note 2 wedge end(s) were moved in z, by at most 1.81763 µm, so each foot lies on its pad: a foot's axis is its pad's top plus half the section's height. The wires' plan geometry and the rest of their loops are as the .wBond states.
note Port 1 ('1') at (-550, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's low-x (left) end (the port's own direction), driving current in the +x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 2 ('2') at (550, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's high-x (right) end (the port's own direction), driving current in the −x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 1 at its line's end is a vertical lumped sheet 100 µm wide and 100 µm tall from 'Pads' down to 'Ground' (the air box's floor): the nearest ground-reference plane with metal under the port.
note Port 2 at its line's end is a vertical lumped sheet 100 µm wide and 100 µm tall from 'Pads' down to 'Ground' (the air box's floor): the nearest ground-reference plane with metal under the port.
note The air box's floor is 'Ground' as a PEC plane at 3 µm: it is the lowest ground-reference conductor, nothing is drawn on it and nothing is drawn below it.
note 'Pads/2' and 1 other conductor(s) are under 3 skin depths thick at 1 GHz, so Thin Metal Correction gives the faces that thickness (2.83 µm on 'Pads/2'). Its resistance levels off at the DC value. Near two to three skin depths a line can still read up to 25 % low. A wide line close to ground can read high, because its faces carry unequal current: up to 20 % on a line 5 times wider than its height over ground, and 50 % at 50 times.
